page.title: Virtual Events Management Guide
page.description: Decide platform, production roles, run‑of‑show, accessibility, and tooling for reliable virtual events.
page.h1: What should you decide first about virtual events management?
page.definition: Virtual events management is the end‑to‑end process of selecting a streaming platform, staffing a live production crew, building a run‑of‑show, ensuring accessibility and backup streams, and coordinating follow‑up tools so an online event runs smoothly from planning to replay.
page.quick_answer: Pick a platform that matches your audience size and budget, assign a show caller and backup stream engineer, schedule a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live, enable captions and a parallel backup feed, and manage the timeline in a work‑management board with a reporting dashboard. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: Which platform type fits my event size and budget?

blocks.p: Match the platform tier to attendee capacity and cost model: self‑serve streaming studios for small webinars, mid‑tier webinar platforms for recurring series, and enterprise event suites for large conferences.

ul: Self‑serve monthly plans such as StreamYard or Livestorm for up to a few hundred attendees
Per‑host licence tiers such as Zoom Webinars that scale with attendee capacity
Annual contract suites such as ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast for thousands of attendees and advanced analytics

sections.h2: What production roles do I need for a reliable live show?

blocks.p: Assign a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, platform operator, and backup stream engineer for anything beyond a simple webinar.

ul: Show caller owns the run‑of‑show and cues every segment
Speaker manager coordinates rehearsals, slide uploads and green‑room logistics
Moderator handles live Q&A, chat triage and audience polls
Platform operator monitors stream health, recording and backup encoder
Backup stream engineer runs a parallel feed on a second encoder

sections.h2: How do I build a run‑of‑show and rehearsal schedule?

blocks.p: Create a detailed run‑of‑show document, schedule a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before go‑live, and run a technical check sixty minutes before start.

ol: Draft run‑of‑show with timestamps, speaker order, media cues and contingency slides
Distribute speaker briefs and branded slide templates at least one week early
Conduct full rehearsal with all roles on the production platform
Run a sixty‑minute technical check covering audio, video, captions and backup stream
Lock final run‑of‑show and share with the crew twenty‑four hours before live

sections.h2: What accessibility and backup plans are required?

blocks.p: Enable closed captions, provide a sign‑language interpreter, and run a parallel backup stream on a second encoder to protect against primary feed failure.

ul: Activate platform‑native captioning or integrate a third‑party caption service
Schedule a qualified sign‑language interpreter for the main stage
Configure a secondary encoder feeding a private backup URL
Test failover by switching to backup stream during rehearsal
Document escalation contacts for platform support during the live event

sections.h2: Which tools manage the project timeline and follow‑up?

blocks.p: Use a work‑management board for the calendar, a brief repository, a publishing CMS, and a reporting dashboard to keep every workstream visible.

faq.q: How far in advance should I lock the venue AV and platform for a hybrid conference?
faq.a: Lock the venue AV and the streaming platform six to eight weeks before the event, before the agenda is final, so production can rehearse on the exact hardware and software that will be used live.

faq.q: What is the minimum crew for a single‑track webinar?
faq.a: One producer can run a simple webinar, handling the run‑of‑show, speaker cues, Q&A moderation and recording, provided the platform offers built‑in captioning and a backup stream option.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Deliver the edited recording and highlight clips within twenty‑four to forty‑eight hours after the live session, while the content is still fresh in attendees' minds.

faq.q: Which platforms support both registration and live streaming in one suite?
faq.a: Zoom Events, Cvent and Bizzabo combine registration, ticketing, live streaming and post‑event analytics, reducing the number of integrations you must maintain.
